A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AAD-LLM study and contain complete main texts and appendices A–F. Textual and visual inspection supports matching the methods, experiments, equations, tables, and figures across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations using six participants' intracranial recordings, speech-only experiments, ablations, and subjective ratings from 40 participants.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds noise-specific results and a neural-window-duration sensitivity analysis.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B retain the same Qwen2-Audio backbone, x-vector clustering, neural speaker predictor, speech separator, attention conditioning, chain-of-thought prompting, and training objectives. The new window-duration experiment introduces no revised algorithm.

E1.justification: The clinical and speech-only datasets, auditory tasks, English-to-Chinese translation, and same-topic Q&A scenarios are retained. Babble and pedestrian noise were already included in v1; v3 reports their results separately. No distinct new dynamic-attention task is specified.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain LTU-AS, SALMONN, Qwen-Audio, WavLLM, GAMA, Qwen2-Audio, and the existing AAD/extraction baselines and oracle controls. The new appendix diagnostics introduce no additional comparator.

E3.justification: v3 adds evaluation over neural-window durations of 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, and 8 seconds in Appendix D.5/Figure 6. Existing data splits, training settings, metrics, and human-rating procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds two focused diagnostics: performance stratified by existing background-noise types and sensitivity of speaker-selection accuracy to window duration. The component, LoRA, feature/clustering, same-topic, and failure-case analyses are retained; the original ablation section moves from D.4 to D.6.

E5.justification: Five speaker-predictor initializations, MOS variability reporting, and the Kruskal–Wallis and Bonferroni-corrected Mann–Whitney tests are retained. The post-hoc tables match after renumbering. The added diagnostics introduce no new run-count information or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Existing results remain unchanged, including 94.4% AAD accuracy in Table 1. New Table 10 reports foreground WER of 10.7% for babble and 17.6% for pedestrian noise. New Figure 6 shows accuracy rising from approximately 35% at 0.1 seconds to 90% at 8 seconds.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, training loss, and Appendix E's speaker-cluster collision argument are unchanged. Adding 'C-channel T-length' explains the existing input notation without revising a definition, assumption, or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same II-ASU framework, brain-guided auditory-LLM contribution, and listener-alignment claims. The new diagnostics do not redefine the principal contributions.

C2.justification: D.4 suggests that unpredictable pedestrian noise causes greater difficulty; D.5 discusses the accuracy–latency tradeoff and adaptive window sizing. The noise interpretation overstates consistency: Table 10's foreground summarization METEOR favors pedestrian noise, 57.2 versus 56.5. Existing limitations and failure explanations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Figure 6 specifies seven tested window durations, adding limited configuration information for the new analysis. Existing implementation, training, hardware, prompts, and code/data access details remain unchanged. Window construction and retraining procedures are not supplied.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. The new appendix analyses add no citations or revised relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v3 inserts two appendix subsections and updates subsequent references, while retaining nearly all existing prose and organization. Small edits clarify input dimensions, remove stray text, and reorder authors. The new window subsection contains an unresolved 'Figure ??' reference.

P2.justification: v3 adds the window-duration plot as Figure 6 and the noise breakdown as Table 10. Existing Figures 6–7 and Tables 10–12 are retained with renumbering and some relocation. The overall two-column design remains, with limited reflow and removal of page-number footers.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the two added diagnostics provide useful evidence about noise dependence and observation-window length. This modest gain outweighs limited reporting flaws: sparse window-procedure details, an unresolved figure reference, and a noise interpretation that overlooks the foreground METEOR exception in Table 10.
